text.title: ui-ux-design.md Template — Worked Examples
text.summary: The five Nielsen heuristics with their one-line tests, the feedback good/bad pair, the required and skipped surface lists, and the six-section outline the template renders.

section.title: The five Nielsen heuristics

list.item: N1 Visibility of system status — "the user always knows what the system is doing right now".
N3 User control & freedom — "the user can undo / cancel / exit without consequence".
N4 Consistency & standards — "the same word means the same thing across the feature and the rest of the app".
N5 Error prevention — "the design makes the bad input hard to enter, not just hard to submit".
N6 Recognition over recall — "the user does not have to remember information from one step to the next".

section.p: Five of the ten Nielsen heuristics are concretely checkable per feature. The other five stay in education material because checking all 10 per feature is theatre.

section.title: The two Norman principles
section.p: Two principles from Don Norman: affordance and feedback. Both are concretely testable per feature; both fix the most common "I clicked it and nothing happened / I did not know I could click it" complaints.

example.note: Submit button: on click, immediately disable + show spinner; on response, swap to success / error state.
Submit button: on click, fire request silently; user clicks three more times waiting for something to happen.

list.item: Web UI — page, component, form, button, modal, navigation.
Mobile UI — screen, sheet, gesture handler.
CLI TUI — interactive prompt, picker, dashboard view.
API-only — REST / GraphQL contracts with no client change.
Data migrations — pure DB schema work.
Internal refactor — input and output unchanged.
Build-system / CI / infra — no rendered surface.
Intent — what the user is trying to accomplish, in one sentence.
Layout — coarse description of element placement; a screenshot or wireframe is allowed but not required.
States — table with one row per state: empty, loading, error, success, disabled. Each row describes the visible affordance.
Nielsen audit — five rows (N1, N3, N4, N5, N6). Each row: heuristic, finding, fix-or-noted-OK.
Copy & microcopy — exact strings for button labels, error messages, empty-state text, success messages.

example.code:
# ui-ux-design: F021 upgrade page
## Intent A signed-in free-tier user upgrades to the solo tier without leaving the account area.
## Layout Plan cards in one row above a Stripe Elements form; primary button below, "Back to account" link under it.
## States | State | Visible affordance | Notes | |----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-------| | empty | cards shown, form hidden, primary button disabled ("Pick a plan") | | | loading | button disabled + spinner, fields read-only | | | error | inline error under card field, form stays editable | no charge created | | success | redirect to /account?upgraded=solo + toast | | | disabled | cards greyed out, "You are already on solo" | |
## Nielsen audit | Heuristic | Finding | Fix-or-OK | |-----------|---------|-----------| | N1 visibility of system status | spinner + read-only fields during submit | OK | | N3 user control & freedom | no cancel after submit | 30s timeout + "Connection lost. Try again." | | N4 consistency & standards | nav says "Upgrade", button says "Choose plan" | rename button "Upgrade to Solo" | | N5 error prevention | card field accepts letters | Stripe Elements mask | | N6 recognition over recall | selected plan repeated above form | OK |
## Norman audit | Principle | Finding | Fix-or-OK | |------------|-------------------------------------------|-----------| | affordance | whole card clickable, only radio styled | hover + pointer on card | | feedback | submit disables + spinner immediately | OK |
## Copy & microcopy | Element | String | |----------------|-------------------------| | primary button | Upgrade to Solo | | empty-state | Pick a plan to continue.| | error message | Your card was declined. | | success | You are on Solo now. |
example.note: Six sections in order, five states, exactly five Nielsen rows, two Norman rows, exact strings. This is the rendered form of the valid example in 02-output-contract.xml.
